sources.claim: Beat 4, quoted: "…Then who will protect you from me?" / "Allah will protect me from you." beats.label: catalog id 25, verbatim
beats.primary: The Expander

A man came in through the mosque door during the Friday khutbah, stood in front of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Allah's Messenger! The livestock are dying and the roads are cut off; so please pray to Allah for rain."

He raised both his hands — "O Allah! Bless us with rain!" — three times. Anas was standing there: "By Allah, we could not see any trace of cloud in the sky and there was no building or a house between us and (the mountains of) Sila."
"A heavy cloud like a shield appeared from behind it. When it came in the middle of the sky, it spread and then rained." They did not see the sun again for six days…
Allah is the One who sends the winds, so they stir up a cloud, then He spreads it in the sky however He wills…

sources.claim: Beat 3 — angels take turns among you, a group by night and a group by day; they assemble at Fajr and at ʿAsr. "Come together" renders وَيَجْتَمِعُونَ (assemble / gather together); an earlier draft's "overlap" was an interpretive gloss and was removed. Quotation marks are used on NO part of beat 3 — it is presented as reported speech, not as a quotation. "Fajr" and "Asr" are used rather than the published "dawn and afternoon prayers" because the Arabic names both prayers explicitly and the app's register uses the Arabic names elsewhere. sources.claim: Beat 6, verse anchor: "And be patient for your Lord's decision — for you are before Our eyes…" — RE-RENDERED FROM THE ARABIC, not quoted from a published translation, per plan §6 rule 2. This is the deck's one deliberate deviation from the batch's Saheeh-International standard. Uthmānī: وَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا. Saheeh International, verbatim: "And be patient, [O Muḥammad], for the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are in Our eyes [i.e., sight]. And exalt [Allāh] with praise of your Lord when you arise". Abdel Haleem, verbatim: "Wait patiently [Prophet] for your Lord's judgement: you are under Our watchful eye. Celebrate the praise of your Lord when you rise." WHY NEITHER IS PASTED: "in Our eyes" is an English idiom meaning in Our estimation / in Our judgement — which is not what بِأَعْيُنِنَا says, and Saheeh International has to append [i.e., sight] to stop the reader making exactly that error. "Before Our eyes" carries the Arabic's sense with no bracket and keeps أَعْيُن PLURAL, which Abdel Haleem's "eye" does not. Abdel Haleem's "under Our watchful eye" was considered and NOT taken: it makes أَعْيُن singular and sharpens the Al-Muhaymin (18) catalogue collision. EXCERPT DISCLOSED ON THE BEAT: a visible trailing ellipsis marks the omitted continuation, "And exalt [Allāh] with praise of your Lord when you arise" — an instruction to praise, containing no warning and reversing nothing. The beat is ENGLISH-ONLY (arabic field empty), per plan §7's convention for new decks.

beats.transliteration: Allahumma Antal-Baqi wa nahnul-fanun faj'al baqaana ta'atan lak

beats.primary: She counted what they still had. He counted what was with Allah. The only part of that sheep that did not last is the part they kept.

sources.claim: Beats 4-5 quotation, verbatim: "What remains of it?" / "Nothing remains of it except its shoulder." / "All of it remains except its shoulder." — the page's published English, checked clause-by-clause against its Arabic (ma baqiya minha / ma baqiya minha illa katifuha / baqiya kulluha ghayra katifiha). No interpolation, nothing bracketed, no attribute clause to adjudicate. In-book ref Book 37, Hadith 56. Darussalam grades it hasan; at-Tirmidhi's own verdict on the same page is sahih. The deck claims only the weaker of the two.
